## Project Summary – SpaceCare: Astronaut Health Monitoring System

SpaceCare is an advanced web-based health monitoring application designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It provides a centralized dashboard to monitor important health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, sleep duration, physical activity, radiation exposure, and mental well-being.

The application allows astronauts to enter health readings, record mood and stress levels, view health trends through graphs, maintain health records, and receive automatic alerts when certain readings require attention. It also supports exporting health reports for further review.

SpaceCare addresses the challenges of spaceflight by helping astronauts identify unusual health changes early and make informed decisions about seeking medical assistance. It is important because prolonged exposure to microgravity, radiation, isolation, and confinement can affect astronauts' physical and psychological health. By bringing multiple health indicators together in one accessible platform, SpaceCare aims to improve health awareness, support early intervention, and contribute to safer and healthier space exploration.

Project Details – SpaceCare: Astronaut Health Monitoring System

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

SpaceCare is a web-based Astronaut Health Monitoring System developed to help astronauts monitor their physical and mental health during long-duration space missions. It provides a centralized dashboard to record and review important health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, sleep duration, physical activity, radiation exposure, mood and stress levels.

Astronauts can manually enter their health readings and wellbeing information. The software stores these records in the browser, displays health trends through graphs, maintains a health history and generates automatic alerts when certain readings fall outside predefined demonstration ranges. It also allows users to export their health records as CSV files for further review.

2. What are the benefits of the project?

  • Helps astronauts monitor multiple health indicators in one place.
  • Encourages regular physical and mental health check-ins.
  • Helps identify unusual changes in health readings.
  • Provides graphs to understand health trends over time.
  • Maintains health records for future reference.
  • Supports sharing health information with medical teams through exported reports.

3. What is the intended impact?

The main aim of SpaceCare is to improve astronaut health awareness and support early identification of potential health concerns during long-duration space missions. It addresses challenges associated with microgravity, radiation exposure, isolation and confinement. Ultimately, the project aims to contribute to safer missions, better health management and improved astronaut wellbeing during space exploration.

4. What tools, programming languages and software were used?

The project was developed using:

  • HTML5: To create the structure of the web application.
  • CSS3: To design the dashboard and provide a modern, responsive interface.
  • JavaScript: To implement health-data entry, calculations, alerts, graphs and interactive features.
  • HTML Canvas: To display health trend graphs.
  • Browser Local Storage: To save health records locally.
  • CSV: To export health records for further analysis.
  • Microsoft Edge: To run and test the application.

No additional hardware or external sensors were required for the current prototype. Health readings are entered manually. Future versions could integrate wearable health sensors and radiation dosimeters.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

SpaceCare combines physical health monitoring, mental wellbeing tracking, health history and automatic alerts in a single astronaut-focused dashboard. Instead of displaying isolated measurements, it organizes different health indicators to help astronauts observe changes over time.

Its responsive interface, interactive graphs, wellbeing check-ins and downloadable health reports make health monitoring more accessible. The project also provides a foundation for future AI-based health trend analysis and integration with space-grade monitoring equipment.

6. What factors did the team consider?

The following factors were considered during development:

  • Space environment: The effects of microgravity, radiation and isolation on astronaut health.
  • Ease of use: A simple interface that astronauts can operate independently.
  • Reliability: Clear recording and presentation of health information.
  • Early awareness: Alerts for readings that require further attention.
  • Privacy: Local storage of demonstration records without transmitting them to external servers.
  • Accessibility: A browser-based application that does not require specialized hardware to demonstrate.
  • Future expansion: The possibility of integrating wearable sensors, medical equipment and AI-based analysis.

Conclusion

SpaceCare demonstrates how software technology can support astronaut health management during long-duration space missions. By combining health tracking, mental wellbeing check-ins, trend visualization and alerts, it provides a practical foundation for improving health awareness and supporting safer human space exploration.

Note: SpaceCare is currently an educational software prototype using manually entered and sample data. Its alerts are illustrative and are not medically validated diagnostic tools.
